edits.old: In order to be able to insert a string at position $i$, we first split the rope at $i$ into two ropes, and then we concatenate the left part, the new string, and the right part.
edits.new:
To insert a string at position $i$, we split the rope at $i$ and
concatenate the left part, the new string, and the right part.
\caption{Inserting text into a rope: one split, then two concatenations.}

edits.old: Rebalancing is cheap enough to run after every few hundred edits.

Because old nodes are never modified, a rope also gives the editor an undo
history almost for free: each version of the document is simply a pointer
to an older root.
edits.new:
Because old nodes are never modified, a rope also gives the editor an

pointer to an older root.
